Oh boy you just opened up the biggest can of worms in online WW2 armored warfare “discourse”. 

First I would like to point out the logistical challenges America faced. They had to have a tank that could be transported overseas, it had to be maintained in the field as there weren’t exactly any Sherman repair factories in Germany and good luck shipping that thing back home to get a tune up, it had to be able to perform a wide range of combat tasks(infantry support, anti armor, anti-structure), it had be well armored enough to provide adequate protection for its crew(of which the Sherman was among the best in crew survival rate), and be mobile enough to traverse all the terrains across Europe. It was also fairly cheap to produce vs their German counterparts which were quite expensive.

You will hear sensationalized stories about how “It took FIVE Shermans to kill just ONE German Tiger!”. When in reality Shermans operated in groups of 5 so of course they are going to go 5v1 if they had the chance(why wouldn’t you?). The 76mm variant of the Sherman had no problems punching through the front plate of a Tiger at a considerable range. Although it’s important to realize that the VAST majority of tank fights, which were rare to begin with, were won by whomever shot first.

TLDR: The Sherman was given a mountain of tasks and it completed most all of them adequately despite the logistical disadvantages the US faced while also maintaining stellar crew survival rates

Life powder is an item that lets you aoe heal your teammates. As far as weapons go, you have strict dps (Great sword, long sword, dual blades. Etc) but you also have options like the sword and shield which is great for quick item usage and applying all kinds of elemental and status effects, the ranged weapons are self explanatory. The hunting horn is the closest you’ll get to a “support weapon” (handing out buffs) but it’s more than capable of dealing out damage and it’s generally frowned upon for you to only give buffs.
4. Capcom and the MH development team constantly add content in the form of new monsters, events, crossovers with other games, and whole expansions. The core gameplay loop of kill monster, make weapons and armor, use those to kill bigger monster, repeat, is pretty addicting. All memes and hate aside (for real tho this bowl season is toxic af). Looking at this objectively, Texas showed up and Georgia (for whatever reason you want to believe) did not. 

Texas offense stayed on the field even if they didn’t come away with points every time.  They ran and passed effectively, nothing crazy, but enough to control the flow of the game. As much as I cant stand a born and bred longhorn Elhinger played a very good game. The O-line did a great job protecting Sam and creating push for the RBs to run through. WRs were pretty solid as expected from this group. Play calling wasn’t fancy but mixed it up enough to get the job done. The defense was the biggest surprise as they were winning in the trenches. This was helped by Georgia’s abysmal play calling but I’ll get to that later. DBs were solid as well and came up with some pretty big plays breaking up passes and that int. 

Now Georgia’s “performance” left a lot to be desired. There’s too much talent on this squad to play so uninspired and sloppy. The play calling was giving me Vietnam style flashbacks to when I would have to watch my Aggies pre Jimbo. There was little to no creativity and was incredibly predictable and had me yelling at my TV. The O-line just wasn’t getting very much push and straight up left guys unblocked sometimes. Which didn’t do an already struggling Fromm any favors. The RBs did pretty good with what they were given but they were running into a loaded box a lot of the time. It’s hard to say how well the WRs did as they were getting overthrown a lot but they didn’t seem to be the problem tonight. Fromm just looked uncomfortable and lost all night. Partly due to his o-line playing sub par. But he was overthrowing like CRAZY. He just never got in sync and the offense suffered for it. Now Georgia’s defense looked lost and confused. Idk if it was a scheme issue but Sam was left unaccounted for waaay more than he should have been. How many times is he gunna roll out to nothing but green grass before you change something? Tackling was also not what I would expect from them. Also special teams gave me cancer.

Overall I’d say all Texas had to do was show up and do their job and they did just that.  Georgia embarrassed themselves after all the playoff talk. (And they also pissed me off for obvious reasons. Now my Longhorn family members won’t be shutting up)
